suggestion.text_hint: put a little aside for the TV licence

sections.title: How things look
sections.text: You are doing fine. January will be a little tight because your TV licence is due, so it is worth planning for.

sections.title: Last month
sections.text: In November, £1,280 came in. Your biggest bills were rent (£480), council tax (£118) and gas (£86). You took out £160 in cash at the Post Office, and you had £230 left over. We cannot see what the cash was spent on.

sections.title: The next three months
sections.text: December looks comfortable, with about £990 spare because you get two pension payments. January looks tight, with about £15 spare, mainly because your TV licence of £175 is due. February looks fine, with about £348 spare.

sections.title: One idea
sections.text: If you put £20 aside in December, January will feel easier. This is only an idea, and it is your choice. Free, independent help is available from MoneyHelper and Citizens Advice.

sections.title: Scam watch
sections.text: Nothing unusual this month. Your payments all look like your normal ones. We will never ask for your details in a letter. If someone calls and asks you for money, put the phone down and use the number on the back of your bank card.

sections.title: Since your last visit
sections.text: Nothing new since we last spoke.

sections.title: Ask a question
sections.text: If you have a question, tick a box on the slip or ask your helper on Tuesday. Priya or a colleague will reply by letter.
